questions.question: What methodology and key metrics are reported for the privacy-preserving clinical language model?
questions.expected_answer: The methodology uses 4-bit INT4 quantization with strict page-level citation tracking. Key metrics show 94.2% citation precision across 200 clinical summaries with factual errors reduced to 1.8%.
evidence: achieved 94.2% citation precision across 200 clinical summaries

questions.question: How do the radiology and clinical language model papers differ in their approach to on-device inference?
questions.expected_answer: The radiology paper uses a cross-attention vision-language backbone for chest X-ray analysis with 91.4% AUC, while the clinical language model paper uses 4-bit INT4 quantization with page-level citation tracking achieving 94.2% citation precision.

questions.question: What privacy concerns do both the radiology and clinical language model papers address?
questions.expected_answer: Both papers address privacy risks of cloud-based inference: the radiology paper emphasizes protecting PHI under HIPAA without cloud transmission, while the clinical language model paper highlights unacceptable privacy risks for protected patient records and clinical trial dossiers crossing hospital firewalls.
evidence: unacceptable privacy risks for protected patient records
